Lower house passes bill on special measures regarding COVID-19 spread

News & Politics (PAP) mr/jch March 03, 2020

In a late evening vote on Monday, the Polish Sejm (lower house) passed a draft law on special measures related to the spread of the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), with 400 MPs in favour, 11 against and 7 abstaining.

The first reading of the bill was held on Monday during the session of the Sejm's health committee. The second was held in the evening, followed by the vote.

The act adopted on Monday will enable employers to order their employees to work from home to counteract the spread of COVID-19 disease.

The proposed law also envisages compensation for parents forced to stay at home in case nurseries, preschools and schools were to be closed.

If an epidemic were to occur, the bill would allow the government to issue an ordinance to close off certain danger zones and establish special measures to apply within these areas.

According to Health Minister Lukasz Szumowski, the act adopted on Monday is "good and necessary" and "complementary to the tools that have been worked on for a long time."

Posted by: Hans Scholl | March 03, 2020"
